entry.title: About
entry.content:
About

microdns is written by Lucas DiCioccio, who blogs at dicioccio.fr. The code is on GitHub at lucasdicioccio/microdns.

This website

This website is generated with kitchen-sink, a static-site generator written in Haskell. The sources live in website/src/ and the published result in docs/, which GitHub Pages serves. To learn more about kitchen-sink itself, see its website and its repository.

Elsewhere

  • kitchen-sink: the generator behind this site.
  • dicioccio.fr: the author’s blog.

entry.title: Dynamic registration
entry.content:
Dynamic registration

Records that are not in the MicroZone file are registered while microdns runs, by calling its HTTP(S) API. They are kept in memory and lost on restart. There are only a few registrations available.

Endpoints

Expose the client IP as A (or AAAA for IPv6 clients) for ${subzone}.${apex}, mostly for the dynamic-DNS problem. The client IP is taken from the x-forwarded-for header if present:

  • POST /register/auto/:subzone?apex=:apex

Expose A or AAAA records (the syntax follows Net.IPv4.decode and Net.IPv6.decode):

  • POST /register/a/:subzone/:value?apex=:apex
  • POST /register/aaaa/:subzone/:value?apex=:apex

Expose TXT ${subzone}.${apex} ${value}, mostly for ACME-challenge tokens:

  • POST /register/txt/:subzone/:value?apex=:apex

Authentication

An HMAC-256 with a shared secret provides a minimum of authentication (see MicroDNS.DynamicRegistration.verifyHmac). Requests carry the header:

x-microdns-hmac: ${base16-encode(hmac(${secret_key},${apex}${subzone}))}

In its present form, the implementation lacks nonces and only hashes the apex and subzone. Queries that can be spied on can therefore be modified and replayed. As a result, if you use the dynamic-registration API over the Internet, TLS should be mandatory.

Note that the apex is the empty string when missing from the URL query parameters: it is not replaced with the one given on the command line. Said another way, the secret key is the only command-line parameter that influences the HMAC.
entry.summary: The HTTP(S) endpoints that add A, AAAA and TXT records to a running microdns, and the shared-secret HMAC that authenticates them.

entry.title: MicroZone files
entry.content:
MicroZone files

microdns uses its own zone-file format, with limited support for DNS records: all TTLs are 300, and there is no support for the CHAOS class, for instance. The file is given with --zoneFile and read at startup; see Getting started.

An example file, with comments, is as follows. It is the repository’s fixtures/example.mzone.

-- comments start with "--"
-- all records have fixed TTL to 300
-- there are no wildcards
-- the @ special syntax replaces the current apex in some records (from the commandline or overriden)
-- otherwise, all domain names are fqdns

-- A and AAAA records
A example.com. 1.2.3.4
AAAA example.com. ::1.2.3.4

-- TXT wants quoted strings
TXT example.com. "microdns has \"quoted\" strings with \\ (backslashes)"
TXT @ "apex syntax"

-- CAA has two quoted strings
CAA example.com. "issue" "letsencrypt"

-- MX

MX example.com. 10 1.2.3.4
MX example.com. 100 spool.example.com.

-- CNAME

CNAME dir.example.com. directory.example.com

-- SRV have only priority
SRV _altweb._tcp.example.com. 10 8080 1.2.3.4

microdns:apex other.example.com.

TXT @ "apex syntax in other.example.com."

The microdns:apex directive changes the apex that @ stands for in the records that follow it; before any such directive, @ is the apex given on the command line with --dnsApex.
entry.summary: The zone-file format microdns reads its fixed records from: the supported record types, the apex syntax, and a commented example.
